The literal "park whenever a hook ran" would park every hook-running commit on this machine and on the owner's, since both select `linux-pgroup` (`apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`). The residual gaps stay as stated: a descendant that runs `env -i` or runs as another user, an escapee behind a failing hook (which reports the hook's own failure), and `macos-tree`. 2026-10-21 (phase 07 unit 25, host gate): the watch no longer depends on the containment driver. A borrowed run is spawned by holder-lock with the descriptor mapped, outside every containment domain, so a `bwrap-pidns` machine is no better placed to see the escapee: the host gate machine selects `bwrap-pidns` (its AppArmor `bwrap` profile grants `userns`; only a confined agent session falls back to `linux-pgroup`) and the owning test reported plain `committed` there 3 of 3. The Git driver now asks for a watched borrow wherever a hook or filter may run, on every driver.
- E5 Git floor: `update-ref --stdin` transactions, `-m`, packed refs, SHA-256, hostile names, `refs/fgos/*` not in default fetch/push. Forge acceptance separate. **P-SYM-HOOK** on this floor, not man pages. Probe shallow clones, clone `--reference`/`--shared` alternates and promisor partial clones for every typed operation; record which are supported, degraded or refused.
- E6 classification of every assertion that reaches a Git write site as kept / retargeted / retired (§15 opening), over the regenerated suite; source-guard false-negative probes for the nine shapes of §12.
- P-SPACE ENOSPC/EIO/permission at prepare/object/pin/CAS/receipt/parent-dir sync, before **and after** the effect, on a real small filesystem (not a shared tmpfs).
- P-RELEASE live old process during activate/rollback; pending newer WAL refused by the activation door (§12); old `fgctl` stopped by the fence; stop-everything cutover for lock-free writers; external project; no legacy-writer fallback.
- P-CUTOVER authorized event-file deletion through the `cutoverGrant` of §7 (borrowed main 50 + WAL exact paths + `refs/fgos/legacy` OID); other tracked `.fgos` still refused, in the same commit and outside it; no env/PID grant; the Event Store ordering of §12 holds.
- P-RESOURCE: at pre-effect and post-effect barriers inject EMFILE/ENFILE, ENOMEM, spawn EAGAIN, output and queue saturation, and deadline cancellation. Required: bounded admission and output, every descriptor closed, WAL/pins/snapshots preserved, no success reported before durability, effect-aware receipts. Ceilings and workload are declared before measuring; a passing budget is never invented afterward.
- Second-load: a second, separate addon load of `fgos-event-store` or `fgos-git` in a Node process that already loaded the combined addon fails closed.

- M1 CAS/recovery: two landers, crash every boundary, later advance, **equal-next OID**, **ABA**, same id / different digest, **cross-resource id**. The winner invariant is per WAL attempt and per uninterrupted expected-state generation, never per OID value over history (§2); each operation publishes at most once. File WAL vs pin disagreement must be **designed out**, not modeled as lawful. Amendment A1 extends M1 to two PublicationCas operations on one ref (§10 rule 4a): crash on both sides of the old target rename after its TargetAttempt, the old orphan git child still able to fire, ABA, equal and differing `next`; required: at most one publication per operation, `superseded` only after the later durable receipt, no attribution beyond WAL evidence; negative controls (supersede without the later receipt or on tip equality alone, supersede with a live old domain, supersede across a different authority, replay of the old CAS) must each give a counterexample.
- M2 ranks/borrow: Node 10/15/30, Git 20/40/50 in a Rust LockScope seeded from the caller's explicit held ranks and verified lease descriptors (option (a)), hook 55, seal 58, state 60, append 70; hook non-wait; no free lock while child writes. Checks the R30 table of §5, including the lease release before land and refusal of a land request that carries 30.
- M3 custody: `dispatch-cwd` lease extended across the runner commit and borrowed into git children; attempt exit, controller death, successor, commit retry; at most one authorized writer; domain-empty currently **false** on Linux/macOS.
- M4 local land success → consumer append fail → retry → cleanup: no second land, operation id preserved.
- P-WAL-ID one transition writer, by the no-overwrite record install of §10, including the loser's stop point and a recoverer that takes over a dead writer.
- P-CUSTODY overlapping writers, with the §6 admission rule.
- C1-C6 are checked separately, each with its own predicate and mapping, never as one label: C1 namespace/hooks by V-PUB and E5 (real backend); C2 by P-WAL-ID; C3 receipt/attribution by M1 and V-CRASH; C4 storage by P-SPACE and E1; C5 release by P-RELEASE; C6 env contexts and matcher by V-TRUST, V-SCOPE and V-SYNC.

## 16. Frozen catalogue: complete disposition

Every G-001..G-234 appears once. Frozen obligation text lives in `plans/reports/research-261017-1032-git-lessons-catalogue.md`; G0's **effective rule** is this section. Precedence: accepted Holder-lock/Event Store, then this G0 replacement (the 32-group override table below), then historical wording. A broad “Carry” is not a disposition when frozen text retains contradictory mechanics.

**Owner amendment 2026-10-20 11:34 — retirement timing.** The event-file dispositions below name the eventual WORK/Event Store cutover, not authorization to drop their assertions during Git caller migration. Until WORK cuts over, retain/retarget those guards through the temporary Work adapter of §§12–13; no event assertion is retired merely because Git phase 07 begins. The frozen catalogue remains unchanged.

**Retired event-file families (D-ADR0055).** Wholly retired: G-089, G-090, G-093, G-118, G-120, G-121, G-170, G-210, G-211, G-212, G-214. Partially retired, with retained non-event obligations: G-029 (event workaround gone; worker `.fgos` strip retained), G-092 (event-file aspect retired; interrupted-merge and native-lock recovery stay in §§9–11, and doctor keeps the detect-only, ownership-aware MERGE_HEAD rule), G-181 (no event-shard stage; Git never writes `.fgos` state payload), G-184 (no production guard-bypass switch), G-213 (event-file guard retired; typed guard-failure diagnostics with a stderr record, an explicit ceiling or streaming for every large blob read, and the rule that a committed-read error never reads as 0 stay in §§2/7, V-TRUST/V-PARITY). G-206 is partially retired by the RT2-F1 override below. Keep G-054/069/086/088/166 (non-event `.fgos`) and all remaining non-event tracked `.fgos` safeguards. Remove old event guards only with actual Event Store cutover. Legacy TTL/PID/heartbeat/unlink lock mechanisms are superseded by unchanged 4.3-R, not recreated in Rust.

**C6 and critique overrides (replace “Carry” on these rows).** 32 row groups: the 14 original groups, 9 added by amendment A1 (23 in all), and 9 added per red-team finding RT2-F1, confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-17. In Appendix A the Disposition and obligation cells of every row in these groups are replaced by the effective rule below; the old frozen text is not repeated next to it and stays only in the catalogue file.

| Rows | Effective rule |
|---|---|
| G-001 / G-183 | Two named env contexts, one backend owner: scrubbed runner; validated hook-index context. |
| `G-027` | Work owns claim reclaim **policy**. Git supplies facts (status, mtimes, branch tips) only. Do not claim reclaim in a Git facts row. |
| G-030 / G-031 | **Execution**, after `worktree-create` returns, outside every Git lock. Git does not spawn `npm` or setup commands. |
| `G-042` | Require dirty-check through destroy under one ownership: worktree-admin 40 wraps add, remove, relocate and prune (holder-lock §16 amended 2026-10-17, owner decision Q6). |
| `G-046` | Guarded cleanup; **no** `finally` force-remove / rm-rf. |
| `G-062` | ScopedCommit and Sync share one commit-failure classification: preserve original commit stderr verbatim; replay only the RepositoryConfig-owned safe guard through Git; never replay a foreign hook. |
| G-071 vs old A §8 | Temporary resolver grant for this merge's scopable conflict paths only; `writeScope` never permanently expands. |
| `G-080` | Consumer verifies; Git binds evidence digest + tree identity; Git does not claim tests ran. Destination never contains an unpublished unverified **Git** merge of an unbound tree. |
| G-166 / G-223 event-file | Event-file deletion only in authorized exact cutover grant after legacy import/verification; retain all other `.fgos` protections. |
| `G-193` | Preserve bytes and session identity; legacy force is not a data-loss bypass. |
| `G-202` | Frozen by owner decision Q5: catchup uses the isolated scoped resolver iff custody; else abort own merge. Land aborts. Catalogue Q16 closed by the owner. |
| G-216 / G-122–G-134 | Kernel Holder-lock supersedes TTL/PID/unlink. Safety lesson (fail-closed ambiguous, no force) retained; mechanism not recreated. |
| G-223 PID-grant / truncation steps | Superseded by D-ADR0055 and Holder-lock borrow verification. Preserve ordering of **surviving** guards. |
| `G-234` | Consumer owns Iron Law/approval; Git binds OIDs/target/evidence. |
| `G-059` | Commit subject and message are consumer-supplied through the ScopedCommit intent; Git validates encoding and length limits and never formats conventional-commit subjects. |
| `G-081` | Workflow's integrate path is deleted in the same release (§13); no best-effort `worktree remove --force`, `rm -rf` fallback or `branch -D` survives; the declared integrate target resolution rule (declared step, else `origin/HEAD`, else checked-out branch) moves to the consumer-side Land intent. |
| G-098 / G-099 / G-102 | Carried unchanged and made explicit in §9 steps 4-5: own-file-set clean gate with whole-repo and subtree scopes, `.fgos` never counts, fail-safe when the set is absent; second check under main 50 immediately before CAS returns `main-checkout-dirty-mid-merge` without moving the ref; after CAS, `read-tree -m -u <old destination> <candidate>` only when the main checkout holds the target, tolerating non-overlapping dirty paths per D-ADR0042 and reporting a lagging checkout in the receipt. |
| `G-100` | Dependency provisioning and setup commands run by Execution after worktree-create and outside every Git lock (same rule as G-030/G-031); a provisioning failure is a consumer verify-fail and never touches main. |
| `G-113` | Ownership re-verification before the critical action is retained; synchronous renew and heartbeat ticks are superseded by unchanged 4.3-R kernel locks (lock-lost-mid-merge is reported from a failed kernel re-check, never from a TTL). |
| G-135 / G-136 / G-137 / G-138 / G-139 / G-140 | v1 `protocol.json` markers, `allowSelfRecognition`, release-if-own unlink, timestamp renew and heartbeat timers are superseded by unchanged Holder-lock; retained lessons: fail closed on unsupported or ambiguous lock state, never unlink, stop-the-world cutover with tombstone. |
| G-161 / G-162 | Hook recognises an fgOS commit only through Holder-lock borrow verification (`run_borrowed`, `FGOS_LOCK_FD` mapped slot); `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID` integer-PID grants are superseded; hook probes once and never waits. |
| `G-175` | Landing and cleanup stay separate phases; branch deletion uses expected-tip CAS deleteRef (§3/§11), never `branch -D`; delivery proof by hierarchical ancestry and TTL anchored at delivered are retained. |
| `G-194` | Existing guards retained (self-mount realpath, HEAD differs from startCommit, status fail-closed); the final step is guarded non-destructive remove with prune, never `worktree remove --force`; one cleanup policy source (G-041). |
| G-032 (override per RT2-F1) | Git worktree-create ends at registration and the worker `.fgos` strip, then returns; it takes no `beforeProvision` callback. Execution provisions dependencies and runs setup after create returns, outside every Git lock (§1, G-030/G-031). Retained lesson: a lock is held only for the narrow Git metadata mutation, and nothing holds main while provisioning runs. |
| G-033 (override per RT2-F1) | Git rolls back only its own create effects: before registration it removes only the operation's own mkdtemp directory; after registration a failed `.fgos` strip unregisters and removes through the guarded non-destructive cleanup of §11 (never `--force`, never `rm -rf`) and rethrows the original cause unmasked. Rollback after a provisioning or setup failure belongs to Execution, which calls the guarded Worktree remove; releasing the runtime claim on create failure is Work/Execution policy. |
| G-095 (override per RT2-F1) | Execution runs the item's verify string through Process in the candidate worktree, outside Git and outside every Git lock (§1, §9). Consumer-side lessons retained: only exit status decides; timeout is configurable (`timeoutMs`), resolves as a typed result and stays distinct from a code failure; stdin ignored; a 10 MiB output ceiling; one configured threshold for every verify path. Git binds the resulting evidence digest and tree identity and never runs verify. |
| G-116 (override per RT2-F1) | Holder-lock kernel open-file-description locks release when the holding descriptor closes, including on process exit; no per-call `releaseOnExit` signal listener is installed. The library never takes over process termination (no `process.exit`) and installs no process-wide handler that kills Node (§5). Release stays an explicit close in `finally`. |
| G-141 / G-142 / G-143 / G-144 / G-145 / G-146 / G-147 (override per RT2-F1) | Lock identity, waiting and holding follow unchanged 4.3-R Holder-lock: registry paths with `dispatch-cwd` keyed by dev:ino after realpath, not v1 `encodeURIComponent` file names; one merge-slot 20 per target ref, so different targets never contend and the slot never replaces CAS; held is retryable named contention, ambiguous or unsupported state fails closed and is never retried, and held asserts nothing about liveness; waits use a monotonic bounded `waitMs` budget covering all retries, with no TTL-derived budget and no 250 ms grace sleep, retrying only the acquire before mutation; verify runs outside every Git lock; no non-slot merge holds main-checkout 50 across merge, verify and commit, and no heartbeat exists; main 50 is taken only for the short main index/tree/HEAD mutation of §9 steps 4-5. Proof obligation retained: a same-target process stays refused for the whole verify while the slot is held (V-LAND, V-ORDER). |
| G-158 (override per RT2-F1) | Superseded by landed 4.4a/4.3-R Holder-lock: `fgos-git` writes no acquire, renew, release, composite-identity, TTL, slot or beacon code in distribution's `lock.rs` or anywhere else, and uses Holder-lock unchanged. Retained lesson: lock constants have one source, checked by Holder-lock's existing tests. |
| G-191 (override per RT2-F1) | Session worktree creation keeps the detached mkdtemp path, the `sessionId` character check before touching any path, realpath nesting refusal and the never-throwing `isSessionWorktree`. Rollback after a failure uses the guarded non-destructive Worktree remove with prune (§11), never `worktree remove --force` and never `rm -rf`; an uncertain state is preserved and reported as recovery-required. Whether this door merges with worktree-create is a migration decision (§13). |
| G-195 (override per RT2-F1) | Every worktree-creating door (claim, dispatch, merge, session, return, workflow, mutation script) goes through one Git create/cleanup operation: `.fgos` strip (G-029), prune after remove, guarded cleanup on failure (G-033, G-041), and serialization under worktree-admin 40, which wraps add, remove, relocate and prune (G-155; holder-lock §16 as amended for Q6). Dependency provisioning (G-030) and setup (G-031) are run by Execution after create returns, outside every Git lock, not by Git. |
| G-206 (override per RT2-F1) | Partial retirement under D-ADR0055: the dispatch attestation guard reads the unified Event Store view, not baseline `events.jsonl` plus `.fgos/events/` writer shards. Retained lesson: "no event found" is distinguished from "valid in-session path" by an explicit signal, never by silence, and every event read goes through one unified reader (Event Store). |

**Compact map (owning contract / vector).** Frozen obligation text is the catalogue file except where the override table replaces the mechanism.

| Lessons | Owning contract | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| G-001–G-017 | §7 driver, parsing, trust (G-001 C6) | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY |
| G-018–G-026 | §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND |
| `G-027` | Work reclaim policy; Git facts only | V-TRUST |
| G-028, G-032–G-043 | §3/6/11 worktree/custody/recovery | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH |
| `G-029` | Partial: strip worker `.fgos`; event workaround gone | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN |
| G-030, G-031 | Execution provisioning, not Git | V-PACK (consumer) |
| G-044–G-049 | §3/9/10 expected-tip refs/WAL | V-CAS/V-LAND/V-CRASH |
| G-050–G-063 | §6/8 scoped commit (G-062 C6) | V-SCOPE/V-PARITY |
| G-054, G-069 | non-event `.fgos` stay | V-SCOPE/V-SYNC |
| G-064–G-079 | §8 Sync (G-071 C6) | V-SYNC/V-CUSTODY |
| G-080–G-088, G-091, G-094–G-117 | §9/10 Land (G-080 override) | V-LAND/V-VERIFY/V-CRASH |
| G-089, G-090, G-093, G-118, G-120, G-121 | Retire event-file D-ADR0055 | V-EVENT |
| `G-092` | Partial: event-file aspect retired; interrupted-merge/native-lock recovery §§9–11 and detect-only ownership-aware MERGE_HEAD doctor rule retained | V-LAND/V-CRASH |
| `G-119` | checkpoint adapter / lockRoot | V-EVENT/V-PARITY |
| G-122–G-134, G-215–G-222 | Holder-lock supersedes TTL/PID/unlink; fail-closed lessons retained | V-ORDER/V-BORROW |
| G-135–G-165, G-167–G-169, G-171–G-180, G-182, G-185–G-201 | Carry per catalogue row into §§3–11/13 as framed by A, subject to precedence; rows in the override table use the effective rule | matching A vectors |
| `G-166` | non-event `.fgos` deletion ban; event-file cutover grant only | V-TRUST/P-CUTOVER |
| G-170, G-210–G-212, G-214 | Retire event-file | V-EVENT |
| `G-213` | Partial: event-file guard retired; typed guard-failure diagnostics with stderr record, explicit ceiling or streaming for large blob reads, committed-read error never 0 retained §§2/7 | V-TRUST/V-PARITY |
| G-181, G-184 | Partial retirement as A | V-EVENT/V-PARITY |
| `G-183` | Hook-index named context (with G-001) | V-TRUST |
| `G-202` | Frozen by owner decision Q5 | V-SYNC/V-CUSTODY |
| G-203–G-209 | Land settlement / cleanup consumer gates | V-LAND/V-CLEAN |
| G-223–G-226 | Hook guards; PID/truncation steps superseded | V-TRUST/V-BORROW/V-ORDER |
| G-227–G-229 | Consumer policy / guarded mutation | V-CONSUMER/V-CLEAN |
| G-230–G-233 | Migration / doctor gate / event field timing | V-PARITY/V-PACK/V-GATE |
| `G-234` | Consumer Iron Law; Git binds | V-LAND/V-VERIFY |

Rows G-135–G-165, G-167–G-169, G-171–G-180, G-182, G-185–G-201 are **not dropped**. Their frozen obligation text and A's per-row port mapping remain in force except where the precedence rule or the override table replaces a retired lock/event mechanism. Appendix A below carries A's per-row matrix with these overrides applied; omitting a G-id is a defect. Structural count 234 (G-001..G-234; freeze line v2.1 adds G-234). Older catalogue header “233” is stale.


E3 typed ScopedCommit (1.5× p95) and Land (1.2× p95) budgets remain **unproven**:
unit 13 does not execute E3. Paired samples alternate legacy/port order to reduce
warm-cache bias; no passing performance claim follows from the script alone.

| G-098 / G-099 / G-102 | Carried unchanged and made explicit in §9 steps 4-5: own-file-set clean gate with whole-repo and subtree scopes, `.fgos` never counts, fail-safe when the set is absent; second check under main 50 immediately before CAS returns `main-checkout-dirty-mid-merge` without moving the ref; after CAS, `read-tree -m -u <old destination> <candidate>` only when the main checkout holds the target, tolerating non-overlapping dirty paths per D-ADR0042 and reporting a lagging checkout in the receipt. |
| `G-100` | Dependency provisioning and setup commands run by Execution after worktree-create and outside every Git lock (same rule as G-030/G-031); a provisioning failure is a consumer verify-fail and never touches main. |
| `G-113` | Ownership re-verification before the critical action is retained; synchronous renew and heartbeat ticks are superseded by unchanged 4.3-R kernel locks (lock-lost-mid-merge is reported from a failed kernel re-check, never from a TTL). |
| G-135 / G-136 / G-137 / G-138 / G-139 / G-140 | v1 `protocol.json` markers, `allowSelfRecognition`, release-if-own unlink, timestamp renew and heartbeat timers are superseded by unchanged Holder-lock; retained lessons: fail closed on unsupported or ambiguous lock state, never unlink, stop-the-world cutover with tombstone. |
| G-161 / G-162 | Hook recognises an fgOS commit only through Holder-lock borrow verification (`run_borrowed`, `FGOS_LOCK_FD` mapped slot); `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID` integer-PID grants are superseded; hook probes once and never waits. |
| `G-175` | Landing and cleanup stay separate phases; branch deletion uses expected-tip CAS deleteRef (§3/§11), never `branch -D`; delivery proof by hierarchical ancestry and TTL anchored at delivered are retained. |
| `G-194` | Existing guards retained (self-mount realpath, HEAD differs from startCommit, status fail-closed); the final step is guarded non-destructive remove with prune, never `worktree remove --force`; one cleanup policy source (G-041). |
| G-032 (override per RT2-F1) | Git worktree-create ends at registration and the worker `.fgos` strip, then returns; it takes no `beforeProvision` callback. Execution provisions dependencies and runs setup after create returns, outside every Git lock (§1, G-030/G-031). Retained lesson: a lock is held only for the narrow Git metadata mutation, and nothing holds main while provisioning runs. |
| G-033 (override per RT2-F1) | Git rolls back only its own create effects: before registration it removes only the operation's own mkdtemp directory; after registration a failed `.fgos` strip unregisters and removes through the guarded non-destructive cleanup of §11 (never `--force`, never `rm -rf`) and rethrows the original cause unmasked. Rollback after a provisioning or setup failure belongs to Execution, which calls the guarded Worktree remove; releasing the runtime claim on create failure is Work/Execution policy. |
| G-095 (override per RT2-F1) | Execution runs the item's verify string through Process in the candidate worktree, outside Git and outside every Git lock (§1, §9). Consumer-side lessons retained: only exit status decides; timeout is configurable (`timeoutMs`), resolves as a typed result and stays distinct from a code failure; stdin ignored; a 10 MiB output ceiling; one configured threshold for every verify path. Git binds the resulting evidence digest and tree identity and never runs verify. |
| G-116 (override per RT2-F1) | Holder-lock kernel open-file-description locks release when the holding descriptor closes, including on process exit; no per-call `releaseOnExit` signal listener is installed. The library never takes over process termination (no `process.exit`) and installs no process-wide handler that kills Node (§5). Release stays an explicit close in `finally`. |
| G-141 / G-142 / G-143 / G-144 / G-145 / G-146 / G-147 (override per RT2-F1) | Lock identity, waiting and holding follow unchanged 4.3-R Holder-lock: registry paths with `dispatch-cwd` keyed by dev:ino after realpath, not v1 `encodeURIComponent` file names; one merge-slot 20 per target ref, so different targets never contend and the slot never replaces CAS; held is retryable named contention, ambiguous or unsupported state fails closed and is never retried, and held asserts nothing about liveness; waits use a monotonic bounded `waitMs` budget covering all retries, with no TTL-derived budget and no 250 ms grace sleep, retrying only the acquire before mutation; verify runs outside every Git lock; no non-slot merge holds main-checkout 50 across merge, verify and commit, and no heartbeat exists; main 50 is taken only for the short main index/tree/HEAD mutation of §9 steps 4-5. Proof obligation retained: a same-target process stays refused for the whole verify while the slot is held (V-LAND, V-ORDER). |
| G-158 (override per RT2-F1) | Superseded by landed 4.4a/4.3-R Holder-lock: `fgos-git` writes no acquire, renew, release, composite-identity, TTL, slot or beacon code in distribution's `lock.rs` or anywhere else, and uses Holder-lock unchanged. Retained lesson: lock constants have one source, checked by Holder-lock's existing tests. |
| G-191 (override per RT2-F1) | Session worktree creation keeps the detached mkdtemp path, the `sessionId` character check before touching any path, realpath nesting refusal and the never-throwing `isSessionWorktree`. Rollback after a failure uses the guarded non-destructive Worktree remove with prune (§11), never `worktree remove --force` and never `rm -rf`; an uncertain state is preserved and reported as recovery-required. Whether this door merges with worktree-create is a migration decision (§13). |
| G-195 (override per RT2-F1) | Every worktree-creating door (claim, dispatch, merge, session, return, workflow, mutation script) goes through one Git create/cleanup operation: `.fgos` strip (G-029), prune after remove, guarded cleanup on failure (G-033, G-041), and serialization under worktree-admin 40, which wraps add, remove, relocate and prune (G-155; holder-lock §16 as amended for Q6). Dependency provisioning (G-030) and setup (G-031) are run by Execution after create returns, outside every Git lock, not by Git. |
| G-206 (override per RT2-F1) | Partial retirement under D-ADR0055: the dispatch attestation guard reads the unified Event Store view, not baseline `events.jsonl` plus `.fgos/events/` writer shards. Retained lesson: "no event found" is distinguished from "valid in-session path" by an explicit signal, never by silence, and every event read goes through one unified reader (Event Store). |

## 17. Acceptance, remaining uncertainty, prohibited claims

G0 has the owner's answers to Q1-Q7 and R30 (§18) and was signed by the owner on 2026-10-18 as D-ADR0057. The first proof runs were folded on 2026-10-18 and re-checked the same day (§19); every finding a re-check reported as violated has a text fix, which is why the owner signed it. What the re-checks established holds only in a finite model or a raw-Git/fixture probe (§19). The second fold's two new rules (§10 rule 4 TargetAttempt; Refs under worktree-admin 40, §3/§5) passed their re-check on 2026-10-18 (§19). The vectors that need an implementation, a real device or owner-written budgets are implementation-time conditions: implementation done requires them to pass. Implementation done requires: boundary-map row; zero product mutation exceptions; one matcher port/implementation; each retained lesson tested at its guard/consumer; all verification vectors with real tests; npm test/Rust suites green. Publication cannot connect before WAL/recovery/doctor exist. Workflow old writer cannot coexist with replacement Land.

**Partial implementation checkpoint, 2026-10-19 (Git phase 02).** The dormant Inspect facade and Rust transaction-local lock scope are present; this does not complete phase 02 or V-ORDER/V-BORROW. Inspect resolves registered linked worktrees only against the caller-supplied trusted main checkout, using its registration instead of worker gitfile contents. Supplying a gitfile checkout itself as that trusted main returns `trusted-main-gitfile-unsupported`, including separate-git-dir layouts, which are not supported by this checkpoint. Unix write snapshots stream hashes under a byte budget and do not follow symlink parents or read special files; other platforms refuse snapshots with `snapshot-platform-unsupported`. Node descriptor handover, non-event Refs/Remote and their Linux mutation proofs are implemented (see §3 and the unit-2 report). Evidence and remaining scope are in [the phase report](../../../plans/reports/phase-lead-261019-0707-git-p02-scope-inspect-refs-remote.md).

No repository evidence shows external consumers using shallow or alternates clones (`scripts/ci-external-consumer.sh` uses neither); the risk that refusing repository-owned layouts until E5 blocks a legitimate clone is unquantified, not observed.

**This text must not be read, and no later revision may be written, as claiming:**

- That the panel approved the spec, or that the owner's answers of 2026-10-17 are a signature; G0 is signed only when the owner signs it, and signing does not pass the implementation-time conditions of §19.
- That any V-/E-/M-/P- vector passed beyond the narrow statement §19 records for it; in particular that M1, M2 or M4 holding in a model abstraction proves an implementation, or that E1, E3, M3, P-CUSTODY, P-WAL-ID or V-CAS passed.
- That the combined addon meets any latency, rollback or packaging budget before E3 and P-RELEASE ran.
- That the R30 table is proven beyond the M2 abstraction (no fairness, bounded wait, cancellation, alias identity or real hook was modelled).
- That concurrent commit safety holds before the `dispatch-cwd` lease extension is implemented and M3/V-CUSTODY pass.
- That holder-lock §16's amended wrap set (add, remove, relocate, prune) is already implemented; it lands with the Git component.
- That `ref == next` proves this operation's CAS.
- That tree equality proves verification.
- That predecessor-domain emptiness is an existing Linux/macOS guarantee.
- That a Git `Custody` entity exists, or that Git acquires, extends or releases the `dispatch-cwd` lease.
- That G-202 was decided in the frozen catalogue (the owner decided it, Q5).
- That “Carry 234” preserves semantics.
- That the 234-row appendix can be copied verbatim with the 14-row override table alone.
- That two separately loaded Rust N-API addons share one in-process `fgos-git` instance.
- That a list of held ranks without a kernel-verified descriptor confers lock authority.
- That land requires a whole-tree clean main checkout (G-098/G-102 own-file set and D-ADR0042 stand, owner decision Q7).
- That G-092 or G-213 is wholly retired.
- That doctor may repair, unlink native locks by age, or treat a bounded scan as complete.
- That a Git receipt authorizes event-segment deletion.
- That a writing noncoding fixture is a production caller.
- That file WAL and op-ref are both authorities, now or “until E1”.
- That a multi-ref `update-ref --stdin` transaction is crash-atomic, on any backend.
- That `core.fsync`, at any setting, makes objects, refs or the WAL durable on stable media; Git does not fsync directories.
- That a process-group kill drains descendants, or that the direct Git child's exit shows the domain is empty.
- That a free `dispatch-cwd` lease after controller death proves generation handoff, or that a successful borrower try-lock proves continuous custody.
- That a recorded handoff over a best-effort domain (`linux-pgroup`, `macos-tree`) proves that no `setsid` or double-fork escapee of the producer still runs (§6).
- That exact-old CAS protects a checked-out branch, or that a checkout snapshot taken outside the worktree-admin 40 hold that covers the CAS protects one.
- That ancestry “no” is an answer when the walk crosses a shallow boundary.
- That a re-check result of 2026-10-18 holds beyond the finite model or probe it ran in, or that the second fold's TargetAttempt and Refs-under-40 rules are proven before their re-checks in §19 run.
- That preflight plus read-back detects a transient symbolic-ref substitution that the `--no-deref` CAS overwrote; the guarantee is containment (§4 C1).
- That exact-old CAS makes a repeated effect harmless, that a target CAS with an unknown outcome may be reissued, or that the CAS winner is defined by OID value over history (§2, §10 rule 4).
- That a multi-ref transaction may carry a target publication as an optimization (§4).
- That a `superseded` PublicationCas ran its CAS, or that it did not; that its CAS may be replayed, reissued or re-attempted under any id; that its id may be reused; or that tip equality, a different authority or an unproven old domain supersedes it (§10 rule 4a).
- That amendment A1 (§10 rule 4a) is proven before its re-check in §19 runs.

## 18. Owner decisions (2026-10-17)

The owner answered every open question on 2026-10-17 at 23:18 (Asia/Saigon), accepting the recommendation on each (“theo khuyến nghị của em cả 8 câu”). These are decisions, not proofs; §19 still gates signature.

| Id | Decision | What it changed |
|---|---|---|
| Missing expertise | No outside experts are engaged. Agents run the proofs (E1-E6, M1-M4, P-*), as for the Event Store. | §19 lists the five expertise areas as risk notes for the agent-run proofs, not as a blocker. |
| Q1 | Topology (a): one combined N-API addon that links both `fgos-event-store` and `fgos-git`, so each Node process has one in-process `fgos-git` load; no per-operation host-process route for Git. LockScope option (a): Rust-owned scope with explicit held ranks and lease descriptors, kernel-verifiable, never a bitmap. E3 gives final confirmation of cost; if E3 shows the combined addon fails a stated budget or rollback with live processes, Q1 reopens. | Header; §4 one-load paragraph and non-publication route; §5 LockScope option (a); §14; §15 V-PACK, E3, second-load, M2. The default dual-addon fail-closed language is removed; a second separate addon load still fails closed. Event Store §3/§4/§17/§20/§21 amended in the signing bundle (2026-10-18). |
| Q2 (N7) | Execution keeps custody by extending the existing `dispatch-cwd` lease across the runner commit, borrowed into git children like other locks; no new Custody entity; Git validates the lease and fails closed when it is missing or stale. The run-supervisor and holder-lock lease change is implementation work in the Git plan. | §2 Custody token; §5 rank 30 row; §6 N7; §14; §15 V-CUSTODY, M3; R30 table. |
| Q3 | The file WAL under the git common dir is the sole recovery authority; `refs/fgos/git-operations` pins are reachability only. No dual write. | §10 authority line; §14 journal row. |
| Q4 | The spec states only the same-release invariant (switch callers and delete the old writers in one release; allowlist zero). The Git plan owns the date. This resolves the brief's contradiction between “order and date” and “no dates”. | §13 date paragraph; §14 Workflow deletion row; §17 claim removed. |
| Q5 (G-202) | With custody, catchup uses the isolated scoped conflict resolver; without custody, it aborts its own merge. Land conflicts abort. Frozen, not recommended. | §8 G-202 paragraph; §14; §16 and Appendix A G-202 rows. |
| Q6 | Holder-lock is amended: `worktree-admin` (rank 40) wraps add, remove, relocate (move) and prune, so the dirty-check through destroy runs under one ownership (G-042, G-155). Still one lock; no second admin lock. | Holder-lock §16 and decision D8 carry the dated amendment; Git §5 rank 40 row and wrap-set paragraph; §11; §16 and Appendix A G-042 and G-195 rows. The named G-042 gap is closed in the design. |
| Q7 | D-ADR0042 is preserved as in amendment A5: own-file-set clean gate, non-overlapping dirty paths tolerated, lagging checkout reported in the receipt. | §9 step 5; §17 claim wording. |
| RT2-F1 rows | The nine RT2-F1 override row groups in §16 are confirmed as written. | “Pending owner confirmation” markers removed from §16 and Appendix A; “(override per RT2-F1)” kept. |
| R30 | The rank-30 versus rank-20 legality table follows from Q1 option (a) and the Q2 lease extension. | §5 R30 table, marked “owner-decided structure, pending model check M2”. |

**Still open** (results, not questions):

1. Proof results: every vector, experiment and model check of §19, in particular E3 (combined-addon cost and rollback with live processes, the Q1 reversal trigger; not yet measurable), E1 (durability claims; not testable without a real device). The re-checks of M1, M3/P-CUSTODY, P-WAL-ID, V-CAS recovery and P-SYM-HOOK ran on 2026-10-18 (§19); V-CUSTODY on the implementation remains.
2. Lending two locks (the `dispatch-cwd` lease and `main-checkout`) to one git child. Owner: Holder-lock. Decision: not needed while runner commits stay in linked worktrees. Holder-lock `run_borrowed` maps one description per child (holder-lock §3), and the R30 table (§5) refuses that combination. Trigger to reopen: a runner commit must target the main checkout; Holder-lock then defines a second mapped slot before Git accepts such a request.
3. RepositoryConfig.ensureFetchMapping now serializes through Git-owned repo-config 80 plus native config.lock. Pre-attempt errors abandon the WAL chain and remove only the invocation's staging inode; post-attempt recovery observes the live refspecs and resolves as effectObservedOnly or uncertain without replay. Hook configuration migration remains with later Git phases; legacy setup hooks still use their existing path.
4. Follow-ups of the signature. Done in the signing bundle (2026-10-18): the component-boundary row (and “pure git integration” removed from Workflow), the Event Store amendment (§3, §4, §17, §20, §21: Publication port in Git, combined addon) and the CHANGELOG line. Still with the Git plan: the program-board row and the calendar date of the Workflow deletion (Q4).

Added by the proof fold of 2026-10-18 (named items with owners; none reverses Q1-Q7):

5. Successor admission on Linux and macOS (§6) has no driver that answers `Empty` until the attempt lock and run-supervisor containment exist. Owner: run supervisor (Execution). Until then admission fails closed and Execution uses a new worktree.
6. The hook support for the event-file `cutoverGrant` (§7) and the ordering with the Event Store cutover (§12). Owner: Git plan, coordinated with the Event Store cutover plan.
7. A public fgOS verb that creates a linked worktree through the Worktree port, so shipped skill text (`fgos-run`) stops telling agents to run `git worktree add`. Owner: Git plan, as its first phase after the Publication port.
8. Whether Workflow runs a read-only workflow in a directory that is not a repository. Git's side is fixed (§1: `notARepository`, never a workflow error); the runner's choice belongs to Workflow and is put to the owner in the fold report.
   Closed (owner answer to plan Q1, 2026-10-18; built 2026-10-21): a Workflow whose Units declare no `writes` runs in a directory that is not a repository, the directory being its own project root; a Unit with `writes` or a sync ref still needs one and is refused before any unit run exists. Proofs: `test/git/e2e-consumer-noncoding.test.mjs` (the read-only route) and `test/runner/execution/run.test.mjs` (the refusal).
9. The consumer settlement uniqueness of §9 step 6 (M4). Owner: Work and Event Store, which confirm the mechanism.
10. The activation door's read contract for unresolved WAL records and the fence for an older `fgctl` (§12 C5). Owner: distribution, with the Git plan; registered before packaging, like the manifest key.

## 19. Proofs required

First proof runs, 2026-10-18 (Asia/Saigon), all against this spec at `59637ba26`, HEAD `1e238aead`, Git 2.53.0, Linux 7.0.0-38, `/tmp` on tmpfs. Run ids: **MC** model check `unit-run-1792254306261-e7f3b8ba`; **DC** durability/cost `unit-run-1792254306560-34bc4761`; **CL** classification `unit-run-1792254306706-087ee956` (read-only, no dynamic run); **GF** Git floor `unit-run-1792257265079-d28a8ade`. **Passed as a vector: none.** “Holds” below means only the narrow statement in that row held in that run; “fixed in §x” means the text was changed by the fold and the fix is **not** proven until its re-check runs.

**Verification vectors** (requirements in §15):

| Vector | Result | Re-check needed |
|---|---|---|
| V-PUB | Raw Git violated: plain `update-ref` ran `reference-transaction`, followed a symbolic `refs/fgos/*` ref to `refs/heads/victim`; `--no-deref` replaced the symbolic ref silently (GF). Fixed in §4 C1 and the hooks paragraph | Yes: V-PUB on the implementation, plus the direct-to-symbolic substitution race (GF did not run it) |
| V-CAS | One winner among competing same-expected CAS held (MC probe, GF, eight contenders, SHA-1 and SHA-256). Violated: a `files`-backend multi-ref transaction killed after the target rename left target = next, pin = expected, `pin.lock` (GF). Fixed in §4 (pin before single-ref target CAS) and the §10 recovery table | Yes: kill between pin and target and inside any multi-ref transaction on `files` and `reftable`, recovery through the WAL |
| V-EVENT | Not run | Yes |
| V-GC | Not run in G0 (V-REF-01 is Event Store evidence) | Yes |
| V-LAND | Not testable: GF ran merge and squash candidates as raw primitives on four clone layouts only | Yes, on the implementation |
| V-VERIFY | Not run | Yes |
| V-CRASH | Raw-Git barriers held for state observation and byte preservation (GF: commit, read-tree, worktree add/move/remove/prune, update-ref). Found: interrupted read-tree cannot be retried (fixed in §10 recovery table); four worktree residue shapes (fixed in §11). Component recovery not testable (no implementation) | Yes |
| V-ORDER | Not run (M2 model only) | Yes |
| V-BORROW | Not run; GF found `setsid()` escapees of hooks and filters (fixed in §5) | Yes |
| V-CUSTODY | Violated in the model and with a real `flock` (MC, M3 witness). Fixed in §6 (admission rule) and §5 (opaque handle, MC F2) | Yes: M3 re-check and V-CUSTODY on the implementation |
| V-SCOPE | Not run | Yes |
| V-TRUST | Raw Git: repository `refs/replace/*` changed `cat-file` for the same OID (GF). Fixed in §4 C1 | Yes |
| V-SYNC | Raw Git held: clean two-parent merge, conflict, abort with byte preservation, continue with parent order, on four layouts (GF). Scoped resolver, foreign abort, custody not testable | Yes, on the implementation |
| V-CLEAN | Raw Git held: dirty remove and `branch -d` of a checked-out branch refused, `worktree repair` kept bytes (GF). Violated: `update-ref -d` deleted the checked-out branch (GF). Fixed in §3 Refs | Yes |
| V-CONSUMER | Paper (CL): domain-neutral, with two holes, a detached-HEAD throw at settle and no rule for non-git projects. Fixed in §1, §13 `integrate.mjs`, §14; runner's own choice is open item 8 | Yes: dynamic run of `business-discussion`, including both cases |
| V-PACK | Not run | Yes |
| V-PARITY | Not run | Yes |
| V-GATE | Violated (CL): no detection rule; nine real code shapes evade a literal scan. Fixed in §12 | Yes: seeded false-negative probes for the nine shapes |

**Experiments:**

| Experiment | Result | Re-check needed |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Not testable (DC): no root, no device-mapper, writable space only on tmpfs. Violated: the hypothesis that `core.fsync=objects,reference` suffices, because Git 2.53.0 fsynced no directory in any traced primitive, even with `all` (DC). Simulated WAL order (file fsync, rename, directory fsync, parent fsync) held at syscall level; ordinary `rename` overwrote an existing record (DC). Fixed in §10 (Git fsyncs directories; no-overwrite install; `processCrash` only until E1) | Yes: E1 on a real device; a syscall trace of `fgos-git` showing the §10 order |
| E2 | Raw-Git barriers held (GF); component not testable | Yes, on the implementation |
| E3 | CLI baseline measured, no verdict because no budget was written before the run (DC, warm tmpfs, single caller): one plumbing spawn p50 5.4-6.4 ms, p95 6.9-7.7 ms; `worktree add` p50 13.1 ms; 100 new refs as 100 processes p50 334 ms against one `update-ref --stdin` p50 12.0 ms; `/usr/bin/true` spawn p50 1.1 ms. WAL model of one 914-byte record per operation: 4,096 allocated bytes per record (about 4.5x), 10,000 records read and parsed in about 46 ms. Combined addon not testable (none built). The Q1 reversal trigger is untouched | Yes: budgets written first, then the combined addon on ext4 with the §15 workload split |
| E4 | Held for same-group descendants (GF). Violated for `setsid()` descendants of hooks and filters, which survived the group kill (GF). Fixed in §5 | Yes: through each platform's containment driver |
| E5 | Held: `start/prepare/commit` and abort, `-m`, exact-old on packed refs, SHA-1 and SHA-256, hostile names refused, custom refs absent from default fetch/push (GF). P-SYM-HOOK violated (fixed in §4). Shallow ancestry false-negative, promisor lazy fetch, missing alternate as generic error (fixed in §2, §4). Reftable held for completed transactions only. Typed `fgos-git` support per layout not testable | Yes: substitution race; reftable fault injection; `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` across every non-Remote operation; `git hook run` on the release floor (§7) |
| E6 | Violated (CL): §13 missed write-site groups, T/T2/T3 undefined, six test files outside every inventory. Fixed in §13 and §15 | Yes: regenerated census and label coverage at implementation |
| P-SPACE | Held before the effect with injected faults: write ENOSPC on a loose object and fsync EIO on a ref lock exited 128 with no ref change; a WAL write fault left a 0-byte temp (DC). Real ENOSPC on a small filesystem not testable (no mount rights). After-effect not run | Yes: real small filesystem, after-effect barriers |
| P-RESOURCE | Not defined in the spec (MC, DC); now defined in §15. Primitive faults observed (DC): EMFILE, MemoryError, short write then EFBIG under `RLIMIT_FSIZE` (fixed in §10: checked writes) | Yes: the §15 definition, end to end |
| P-RELEASE | Paper (CL): stands only as stop-everything; no owner of the rollback check. Fixed in §12 | Yes: live old process during activate and rollback |
| P-CUTOVER | Violated (CL): no grant mechanism for the event-file deletion commit of Event Store §18; unstated ordering with the Event Store cutover. Fixed in §7 and §12 | Yes |
| Second-load | Not run | Yes |

**Model checks** (MC; explicit-state BFS to an empty queue, bounded abstractions, process-crash profile):

| Model | Result | Re-check needed |
|---|---|---|
| M1 CAS/recovery | Held: distinct-next 1,097 states, equal-next 1,769, ABA 1,833; no double publication, at most one CAS winner, no publication before durable WAL. Target + pin was modelled as one atomic step, which the V-CAS fold no longer assumes | Yes: re-run with pin and target as separate steps and crash between them |
| M2 ranks/borrow | Held: 266,240 cases (2,048 held-rank subsets × 26 profiles × 5 descriptor states); no two-scope wait cycle (2,187 states). Hook modelled as a single probe | No model re-check; V-ORDER still required |
| M3 custody | Violated: “controller dies → successor acquires free lease” with a live producer descendant without the lease fd; reproduced with real `flock` and pipe barriers. Borrowed git child excluded correctly. Fixed in §6 | Yes: with the admission rule; the counterexample must become “refused” |
| M4 land → append failure → retry → cleanup | Held for a failure known to precede its effect; held with dedup for an unknown outcome; negative control without dedup gave two settlements. Fixed in §9 step 6 (consumer contract) | Yes, once Work/Event Store confirm the mechanism (open item 9) |
| P-WAL-ID | Not testable: no primitive was named; the negative control without exclusion had two transition writers. Fixed in §10 (no-overwrite record install) | Yes |
| P-CUSTODY | Violated, same witness as M3 (real kernel). Fixed in §6 | Yes, with M3 |
| C1 namespace/hooks | Not testable in the model (truth table only); covered by V-PUB/E5 above | Through V-PUB/E5 |
| C2 operation records | Not testable; depends on P-WAL-ID | Through P-WAL-ID |
| C3 receipt/attribution | Held in the abstraction: equality creates no publication; recovery only observes | Through V-CRASH |
| C4 storage/capacity | Held in a logical-barrier model; not a power-loss or filesystem proof | Through P-SPACE/E1 |
| C5 release | Not testable (truth table only) | Through P-RELEASE |
| C6 env/sync | Not testable (context selector only; no matcher or hooks) | Through V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-SYNC |
| SafeRestore / no force | Held in a six-state model: original bytes or a durable snapshot always survive | Through V-CLEAN/V-CRASH |
| Borrower test (MC F2) | Finding: the three-condition test passes on a never-locked description. Fixed in §5 | Through V-CUSTODY |

**Re-check runs, 2026-10-18 (Asia/Saigon).** All five read this spec at `b6bd66cfd` (SHA-256 `a27c61e7…f247`), HEAD `6c1ebfe19`, Git 2.53.0, Linux 7.0.0-38, `/tmp` on tmpfs; none wrote to the checkout. “Held” means held in the stated finite model or probe, never on an implementation. Text fixes below are the second fold of the same day.

| Vector | Run | Result | Text fix (second fold) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 CAS/recovery | `unit-run-1792258831537-27d2052d` | Held with pin CAS → read-back → prepared → target CAS as separate steps: distinct-next and equal-next 289 states each, crash at all six internal boundaries, no double publication, no attribution without WAL evidence; record-0 binding refused a different digest and a different resource set in both install orders. Violated: (F1) a recovery that retries on `ref == expected` after an ABA publishes twice (9-step trace); (F2) “one winner per expected OID” fails across an ABA (11 steps, correct Git semantics); (F3) a multi-ref optimization that installs the target before the pin publishes before prepared (2 steps) | F1, F2: §2 winner per WAL attempt/generation; §10 rule 4 TargetAttempt and recovery rows; §15 M1. F3: §4 optimization deleted | Held in model; fixes 1-2 need the re-check below |
| M3 / P-CUSTODY | `unit-run-1792258831682-809bcfd3` | Held in a finite model (no handoff, no driver: 24 states, 30 edges; driver proving `Empty`: 31, 39) with no overlapping writer after admission; the old rule still reaches “controller dies → successor admitted” in 2 steps. Real `flock` probe 20/20: two lease-less writers (one `setsid`) write while the successor holds the free lease, and the admission rule refuses with `custody-predecessor-unknown` and a new worktree. A never-locked description passes the old try-lock and is refused as a non-acquired opaque handle. Commit retry keeps the lease; handoff follows the receipt | None needed | Held in model and fixture probe; V-CUSTODY on the implementation remains |
| P-WAL-ID | `unit-run-1792258831821-6bcbac29` | Held in a finite model (36 configurations, 89,026 states): one transition writer per record number, the loser stops at `EEXIST`, a different digest or resource set is refused; negative controls (overwrite, no stop point, no binding check) all fail. Probe on tmpfs: `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` and `link`+`unlink` gave one winner and two `EEXIST` in each of 100 rounds × 3 writers; a SIGKILL between `link` and `unlink` left both names on one inode and the retry got `EEXIST`. Violated: exact-old CAS + ABA + retry of an unknown outcome gives two effects; a recoverer holding the resource authority that replays blindly after a crash before the receipt gives two effects | §10 rule 3 (CAS alone is not enough) and rule 4 (TargetAttempt; observe before any re-effect) | Held in model/probe; fix 1 needs the re-check below; no stable-media claim |
| V-CAS recovery | `unit-run-1792258831977-3ff6a365` | Held: SIGKILL of a coordinator after pin, read-back and WAL fsync left target = old, pin = next on `files` and `reftable`; `files` multi-ref still not crash-atomic (target = next, pin = old, `pin.lock`); `reftable` showed no partial visibility at its two measured barriers (not generalized); kill at `reference-transaction` prepared left old/old with native locks; every observed state was decided by the §10/§11 rules from a simulated WAL without unlinking a lock by age or PID and without replaying or rolling back the target; an owned `pin.lock` quarantine with inode recheck repaired the pin. Violated: `update-ref -d` with exact old deleted a branch checked out by a worktree registered after the snapshot (both backends); the optimization sentence allowed pin and target in one transaction | §3 Refs and §5 rank 40 and R30 Refs row: revalidation under worktree-admin 40 through the CAS; §11 delete; §4 optimization deleted; §10 residue row reworded | Held in raw-Git probe; fix 3 needs the re-check below |
| P-SYM-HOOK / V-TRUST | `unit-run-1792258832134-b64a7405` | Held: containment, `--no-deref` CAS with expected OID left every `refs/heads/*` unchanged in the substitution window (control without `--no-deref` moved the victim); seven Publication primitives with a trusted empty `core.hooksPath` fired no `reference-transaction` hook (control fired `prepared`, `committed`); `--no-replace-objects` reads returned original objects despite `refs/replace/*`; `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` blocked lazy fetch for status (rename detection), diff, cat-file, checkout and fast-forward merge in a promisor clone (controls fetched); `git hook run pre-commit` exists on 2.53.0. Violated: preflight + read-back did not detect a transient symbolic substitution that the CAS overwrote (a symbolic ref still present at read-back was detected) | §4 C1: containment is the guarantee; transient detection not guaranteed; §15 V-PUB; §17 | Held in raw-Git probe; no detection mechanism claimed |

**Re-check list after the second fold** (fixes 1 and 3 only; the other fixes delete or narrow a claim): M1 and P-WAL-ID with the TargetAttempt rule of §10 rule 4, where the retry-on-ABA counterexample and the blind replay with resource authority must become `recovery-required`, and recovery may re-attempt only by installing the first TargetAttempt; the Refs-under-40 rule, where a worktree registered between snapshot and CAS must be refused, and M2's delta for the new rank-40 Refs profile.

**Second re-check runs, 2026-10-18 (Asia/Saigon), spec at `f713c4204`.** `target-attempt-recheck` (`wf-run-1792262850536-7f974cb3`, unit `unit-run-1792262850667-7d04943f`): held in a finite model (12 configurations, up to 1,345 states each); the earlier 9-step retry-on-ABA trace and the blind replay with resource authority both end in `recovery-required` with exactly one publication; a live writer and a recoverer racing to install the first TargetAttempt yield one winner, the loser stops at `EEXIST` before any effect; negative controls (retry marker, blind replay under lock, overwrite, no `EEXIST` stop, attribution before outcome) each produce a counterexample as expected. `refs-under-admin-recheck` (`wf-run-1792262850691-bb0a3004`, unit `unit-run-1792262850821-1cb9027c`): held in a finite model for delete and advance with a concurrent Land and a concurrent worktree add, in M2 with the rank-40 Refs profile (no wait cycle), and on real Git with `files` and `reftable` when both sides take the lock: a worktree added before revalidation makes the Refs operation refuse, and an add waiting on 40 fails afterwards because the branch is gone. The one counterexample reproduced is a writer that adds a worktree without taking 40 (raw Git outside fgOS): the exact-old delete succeeds and read-back only detects it. That writer is outside the cooperating-writer assumption and is excluded by the mutation allowlist reaching zero and the source guard of §12 (V-GATE), which are implementation-time conditions.

**Re-check required for amendment A1** (owner, 2026-10-18; §10 rule 4a; pending, none has run). Each runs on this text before Git phase 01 freezes its Publication interface:

**A1 re-check results, 2026-10-18.** `a1-model-recheck` (`wf-run-1792294509927-9dd08319`, unit `unit-run-1792294510062-7dffd95e`): held in a finite model (131 states per safe configuration) for two PublicationCas on one ref with equal and different next, the recoverer/superseder race (loser stops at `EEXIST`, terminal id never rebound) and the refusal before Intent when the borrow is unavailable; every negative control (no receipt, tip equality only, volatile receipt, live old domain, other authority, replay) produced its counterexample. It found that a raw kernel acquire does not prove the old domain gone on Windows (4-step trace); rule 4a now requires the holder-lock §8/§8.1 admission. `a1-vcas-recheck` (`wf-run-1792294510067-c73acc31`, unit `unit-run-1792294510203-3f2a2156`): real Git 2.53.0 on `files` and `reftable`, kill after TargetAttempt and after the target rename both end with the new operation winning and the old one `superseded`, nothing pending; kill just before the rename fails closed on the retained backend lock until the §11 exact-owned quarantine; a borrowed orphan child blocks the new acquire until it exits, and an unborrowed child is the counterexample rule 4a forbids. Reftable leaves `tables.list.lock`, not `<ref>.lock`; rule 4a now names backend native lock artifacts. Implementation conformance (Rust/Node Publication, the Event Store kill matrix) remains an implementation-time condition.

1. **M1, two operations on one ref.** Old PublicationCas killed on both sides of the target rename after its TargetAttempt, its orphan git child still able to fire, an ABA control, equal and differing `next`, then a new operation id under the same event-seal. Required: at most one publication per operation, no attribution beyond WAL evidence, `superseded` only after the later durable receipt. Negative controls, each of which must give a counterexample: supersede without the later receipt (including on tip equality alone); supersede with the old domain live; supersede across a different authority; replay of the old CAS.
2. **P-WAL-ID.** A recoverer of the old id racing the install of the `superseded` record: one transition writer, the loser stops at `EEXIST` before any effect, the old id is never rebound.
3. **V-CAS on `files` and `reftable`.** Real Git with SIGKILL and syscall barriers: a stale TargetAttempt of a PublicationCas, killed before and after the target rename, followed by a new operation on the same ref; the new operation proceeds, the old is closed `superseded` only when rule 4a holds, no CAS is reissued, no unresolved record remains, and a retained `<ref>.lock` or a live old domain keeps `recovery-required`. On the implementation, Event Store §23.2 item 1's kill matrix (kill after object write and around `update-ref`) show no stalled seal and no unresolved record.

**Missing expertise** the council could not supply. Owner decision (2026-10-17): no outside experts; agents run the proofs, as for the Event Store. These areas are where an agent-run proof most needs care:

1. Git reference-backend internals on the release Git floor (files and reftable backends, reference-transaction hook firing, symbolic-ref dereference modes, replace-object handling, and alternates/shallow/promisor object availability).
2. Filesystem power-loss durability testing (per-filesystem fsync semantics, device-mapper fault injection, parent-directory durability).

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text:
1. **M1, two operations on one ref.** Old PublicationCas killed on both sides of the target rename after its TargetAttempt, its orphan git child still able to fire, an ABA control, equal and differing `next`, then a new operation id under the same event-seal. Required: at most one publication per operation, no attribution beyond WAL evidence, `superseded` only after the later durable receipt. Negative controls, each of which must give a counterexample: supersede without the later receipt (including on tip equality alone); supersede with the old domain live; supersede across a different authority; replay of the old CAS.
2. **P-WAL-ID.** A recoverer of the old id racing the install of the `superseded` record: one transition writer, the loser stops at `EEXIST` before any effect, the old id is never rebound.
3. **V-CAS on `files` and `reftable`.** Real Git with SIGKILL and syscall barriers: a stale TargetAttempt of a PublicationCas, killed before and after the target rename, followed by a new operation on the same ref; the new operation proceeds, the old is closed `superseded` only when rule 4a holds, no CAS is reissued, no unresolved record remains, and a retained `<ref>.lock` or a live old domain keeps `recovery-required`. On the implementation, Event Store §23.2 item 1's kill matrix (kill after object write and around `update-ref`) show no stalled seal and no unresolved record.

2. Filesystem power-loss durability testing (per-filesystem fsync semantics, device-mapper fault injection, parent-directory durability).

5. macOS and Windows kernel file-locking and process containment (`holders()` unlistable; Windows driver not activated; Linux/macOS predecessor-domain gap).

Kiểm tra: tip có seq thấp hơn mốc là `regressed`; log mất đuôi có seq là `log-emptied`; không dòng nào mang seq của mốc là `mark-seq-missing`; dòng tại seq đó khác hash là `content-mismatch` (bắt được cả khi log đã mọc lại quá mốc); chưa có mốc thì `bootstrap`; chỉ khi kiểm tra sạch mốc mới được tiến; dòng cuối không parse được thì từ chối đánh dấu thay vì đánh dấu hỏng; đuôi cũ không có seq thì không có gì để đánh dấu. Khi một file có break chưa được xác nhận: mốc đứng yên ở vị trí tốt cuối, cảnh báo được ghi (`recordMainCheckoutGuardWarning`), commit dự phòng bị từ chối khi BẤT KỲ file nào có break (break ở shard của một writer nghiêm trọng như baseline); không có tự sửa, xác nhận là lệnh thủ công riêng (`--force-rebaseline-all` ghi mốc tip hiện tại cho mọi file có thật, báo `skippedEmpty` cho file không có đuôi seq). |

Component ghi sidecar nguyên tử, tuần tự hóa đọc-sửa-ghi, KHÔNG coi sidecar hỏng khi đã có bằng chứng cắt xén là bootstrap im lặng, và doctor không ghi trạng thái. |

Khoảng: tham số kiểm thử, rồi `checkpoint.fallbackIntervalSec` trong `.fgos/config.json`, rồi mặc định 3600 giây. Pathspec gồm `.fgos/events.jsonl` và thư mục `.fgos/events`, dấu phân cách đổi `\` thành `/`. Đếm sự kiện chưa commit cộng cả baseline-0 lẫn mọi shard. |

Safety lesson (fail-closed ambiguous, no force) retained; mechanism not recreated. |

Verb `unclaim` của người: không có claim thì `{released:false}`, trạng thái bền không phải `doing` thì xóa vô điều kiện, `doing` còn hoạt động mới thì từ chối nêu người giữ, đã yên thì xóa với `stale-liveness`, claim của writer khác thì phải đủ quyền (tsk-uio). |

Superseded by D-ADR0055 and Holder-lock borrow verification. Preserve ordering of **surviving** guards. |

The Inspect driver exposes `hash_object(repo, ObjectType, bytes)` for blob, tree and commit identities. It runs `git hash-object -t <type> --stdin` through the existing read-only command door, without `-w`, installing no object and borrowing no publication authority.

| G-007 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Resolve base bằng `rev-parse -q --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`; kết quả null nghĩa là 'không trỏ tới commit nào' và bị từ chối trước khi có run. |
| G-008 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Lệnh con kết thúc theo sự kiện thoát của chính child trực tiếp, và timeout phải thực sự chặn được thao tác kể cả khi hậu duệ giữ descriptor. docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ### Phase 06 unit 10 recovery review notes
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
### Phase 06 unit 10 recovery review notes

Native quarantine compares the moved file's device/inode after rename. A
substitution is restored with a no-overwrite hard link; if the original path
is occupied, both paths are preserved and the inspection report identifies
the retained quarantine path. This does not claim successful repair.

Config recovery intentionally preserves config.lock if a writer dies after
writing bytes but before appending the updated NativeLockOwned capture:
intent-time empty-file evidence no longer matches. Inspect the retained WAL,
config.lock and local config before manual repair; a new config operation
cannot bypass this unresolved evidence. Hooks removal uses --fixed-value,
which Git supports since 2.30, below the declared 2.53.0 floor.

Hooks provenance uses an optional WAL ConfigChange configSequence, assigned
under repo-config authority from retained config history. Directory mtimes do
not establish ownership order. Historical digests omit this field; ambiguous
latest historical provenance refuses ownership. Config provenance chains remain
retained and inspection remains bounded by 100,000 chains (L4).

Phase 06 unit 11 adds `packages/git/rust/tests/recovery_matrix.rs`: all twelve
Recovery payload kinds run through their real operation ports and receive
SIGKILL immediately after the directory fsync installing Intent. Each kind is
run twice, with Recovery first and with the owning recovery port first. The
matrix checks pending discovery, kind/intent inspection, the terminal
`abandonedBeforeAttempt` outcome, and request-digest/outcome retention after
compaction. Restore uses its acknowledgement; Land and Publication use their
own cleanup; other uncompacted cases use the existing WAL compactor while
holding the owning resource and reading real refs. This establishes the
pre-attempt row for every kind, not every internal or post-effect crash point.
Compacted Recovery returns the retained Outcome; a typed owning port such as
Sync may reconstruct a different response shape with the same terminal state.

Acceptance remains incomplete. The borrowed spawn port still lacks a
pre-execution identity callback; index ownership's production producer remains
unresolved (the fixture recorder is crate-private and test-only). Process
identity recorded before exec is necessary but does not alone attribute an
inode: a foreign Git can create index.lock after the absence check and before
the stopped child resumes. No such residue may be adopted merely because the
recorded child later died. Native repair callers must not be wired until both
the spawn boundary and artifact attribution are established.

### Cooperative termination host acceptance

Real Git read-tree/index.lock cleanup tests live in the Git crate’s
`borrow_deadline` suite; holder-lock retains generic cooperative/forced deadline
coverage. Readiness budgets allow five seconds for the generic handler and eight
seconds for Git’s filter (ten-second Git deadline).
The Linux namespace-init case is explicitly ignored in ordinary runs. An eligible
host must run this exact merge gate, which fails if its bwrap probe fails:

```sh
cargo test -p fgos-git --test borrow_deadline real_read_tree_deadline_as_namespace_init_cleans_its_native_lock -- --exact --ignored --nocapture
```

An ignored test is not passing acceptance evidence. Full `npm test` and E3 remain
separate required host merge gates.

docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.title: 1. Purpose
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sample: 1. Purpose
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.text: ## 1. Purpose
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sectionText:
## 1. Purpose

A run supervisor is one Rust process per attempt. It owns the attempt after the controller (the Node process that ran `fgos run`) handed it over, so a controller that dies, hangs or is killed no longer loses the result of a CLI agent. The agent keeps running, its result is settled, its credential is written back and its home is cleaned, with no one resuming it.

Two roles, one contract set:

| Role | Process | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Supervisor | `fgos internal supervise` | Holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the gate, watches deadlines, publishes the receipt, runs the steps |
| Gate | `fgos internal gate` | Is the process root of the agent inside the domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux), owns the agent's IO, enforces the hard ceiling, ends the domain when the agent is gone, publishes `gate-exit.json` |

Adopt (`fgos internal adopt`, section 8) is the third entry point: it settles an attempt whose supervisor is gone.

docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.text: ## 2. Ownership boundary
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sectionText:
## 2. Ownership boundary

| Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|
| Envelope v3 and its digest ([contract](../../../packages/run-supervisor/contracts/envelope.v3.json)) | Which executor, model or argv runs (Execution Core `bind()` and `resolveExecutorCommand`; the argv is written into the envelope) |
| The layout of an attempt directory and the one-time publication of its files (section 3) | Judging the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the `settle-attempt` step) |
| Binding, GO, gate-exit, stop and cancel requests, receipt, step receipts, closed marker | Retry, fallback or the next attempt (controller) |
| The post-receipt step runner (section 7) | What a step does (the Node payload defines `settle-attempt`, `finalize-home`) |
| The adopt door and its recovery matrix (section 8) | The attempt lock primitive (holder-lock) and the containment port (process control) |
| Deadlines: soft and idle by the supervisor, hard ceiling by the gate | Panes, tabs, placement (terminal-control; the supervisor addresses a pane only by the attempt id, as a key) |
| The four internal routes and their protocol (section 10) | Any verb a person calls |

Layering: the gate and supervisor are L4. They use the containment port and facts of `fgos-process` (L0), the attempt lock and predecessor record of `fgos-holder-lock` (L1) and the adapters of `fgos-agent-protocol` (L3). Nothing below knows an attempt. The component-boundary entries are in [component-boundary.md](../component-boundary.md#4-current-high-level-components).

The `BoundInvocationSupervisor` of `packages/host-runtime` is a different thing: a short RPC call bound to its caller's lifetime. It stays separate; only L0 primitives are shared.

docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.title: 3. Attempt directory and publication
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sample: 3. Attempt directory and publication
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.text: ## 3. Attempt directory and publication
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sectionText:
## 3. Attempt directory and publication

Layout (all names from the envelope contract; `<attemptDir>` is `<assignmentDir>/runs/<NN>`):

| File | Written by | When |
|---|---|---|
| `attempt.lock` (+ `.predecessor.json`) | controller creates, supervisor declares the domain | Registry row `attempt`, rank 15, kind lease |
| `envelope.json` | controller, once | After the locks are held, before any agent process exists |
| `protected/attempt-secrets.json` (0600, dir 0700) | controller | Secret env and run-control token; never copied elsewhere |
| `supervisor-binding.json` | supervisor | After the gate runs inside the domain, before GO |
| `gate-exit.json` | gate | After the agent exited and the domain was emptied. Inside a sandbox with a read-only root the controller leaves an empty `gate-exit.json` bound writable (as the two capture files) and the gate fills it in place, never through a symlink; no process of the agent exists then, so the gate has the last word |
| `stop-requested.json` | supervisor | Before SIGTERM to the gate |
| `cancel-requested.json` | anyone allowed to cancel | Polled by the supervisor |
| `receipt.json` | supervisor, or adopt | After the gate is gone |
| `steps/<stepId>.json` | step runner | Only after the step exited 0 |
| `closed.json` | supervisor, or adopt | When every step has a receipt |
| `adopting.json` | adopter | While it holds the lock |
| `start-refused.json` | supervisor | Only when it ends before binding: `{attemptId, code, why}` (`lock-held`, `lock-unavailable`, `envelope-invalid`, `host-version-mismatch`, `internal`). Adopt shows the `code` |
| `supervisor.log` | supervisor stdout and stderr | Free text, never parsed |

The supervisor also writes `agent-binding.json` (the agent's tuple from the gate's AGENT frame) and `supervisor-heartbeat.json` (display only, every 5 s). Neither is in the layout contract; nothing decides from them.

**Publication rule.** Every file except `supervisor.log` is written to a temp file in the same directory, fsynced, then hard-linked to its final name. `EEXIST` means another writer already published it: read that one, never overwrite. `adopting.json` is the one exception: it describes only the current holder and is replaced by temp file and rename.

**Digest.** `envelope.digest` is `sha256:` plus the hex sha256 of the canonical JSON of the envelope without the `digest` key (keys sorted by UTF-16 order, integers only, no whitespace). Node (`canonicalJson` in `src/runner/dispatch/proof-helpers.mjs`) and Rust (`fgos_run_supervisor::envelope::digest`) reproduce the shared [vector file](../../../packages/run-supervisor/contracts/vectors/envelope-digest.v1.json) byte for byte. A reader finding `v != 3` or a wrong digest treats the run as `legacy-run` (adopt) or refuses with `envelope-invalid` (supervise, gate, attempt-step).

The envelope is immutable and carries no secret. It names: `attemptId`, `unitRunId`, `runDir`, `mode` (`direct` or `terminal`), `protocolId` 1, `hostBin` and `payloadRoot` of the release that wrote it (resolved once, never through PATH or a shim), `cwd`, `mutation`, `launch` (command, args, non-secret env, `stdinPolicy`, `briefPath`, `outboxDir`, capture paths), `containment.preferred` and `bwrapPrefix`, `deadlines`, `agentProtocol.cli`, and the `steps`. In `terminal` mode it also names `slot {key, groupKey}`, `terminal {socketPath, exitCommand, orphanSettleMs, retainFailedPaneMs, briefPath, outboxDir, groupKey}` and `identity {writerId, parentWriterId}` (section 5.3); `identity` is also written in `direct`. A `createdAt {bootId, boottimeNs}` field lets Windows adopt give an unbound attempt a 60 s start grace on the same boot; file times are never used.

docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.title: 4. Handover: controller to supervisor
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sample: 4. Handover: controller to supervisor
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.text: ## 4. Handover: controller to supervisor
docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md.sectionText:
## 4. Handover: controller to supervisor

1. Mint the attempt id and create the run directory. Acquire the attempt lock (rank 15). A writing Unit supplies its already-held dispatch-cwd lease (rank 30); every round and provider failover reuses that same acquired handle. A standalone writing Assignment acquires 30 after 15 in its attempt scope. A read-only attempt takes no cwd lease. Refused: the attempt does not start.
2. Prepare: bind, `confinement.prepare` (home marker v2 carries the attempt id), write the envelope and the side file.
3. Spawn `$hostBin internal supervise --envelope <path> --protocol 1` with the attempt lock at fd 3 and the lease at fd 4, `setsid`, stdio to files, **no IPC channel and no pipe**. (Windows: the controller releases only the attempt lock so the supervisor can take it. Its existing lock-hold helper retains the cwd lease; `cwdLeaseOwner` names its private existing request channel. The supervisor declares its producer job through that helper and must receive `declared` before GO. A dead helper cannot acknowledge a late start; a helper that dies after acknowledgement leaves the declared domain for successor admission. Supervisor death still leaves the producer running for adopt. **Windows controller death differs intentionally, fail-closed:** its helper exits and frees the cwd lease; successor admission can then terminate the recorded producer job before an adopting controller resumes it. A `LockFileEx` lock belongs to the acquiring process, so the supervisor cannot acquire an independent exclusive copy alongside that helper through the current port. The acknowledged declaration is retained; no second acquire or unacknowledged GO is introduced. Unix supervisor/gate copies retain the lease and preserve adoption after controller death.) The envelope names `cwdLeaseFile` on **every platform**; the supervisor writes its domain in that lease's existing predecessor record before GO.
4. Wait for `supervisor-binding.json`. A wait that ends without it is `launch-unknown`, never `not-started`: the attempt stays for adopt, which concludes only when the lock is free and the domain is empty.
5. On binding the controller closes only its attempt copy. It retains the cwd lease through the last runner commit, receipt and handoff; commit git/hook children receive it through holder-lock `run_borrowed`. After observing the producer domain empty and persisting the result, it calls `clearDomain()` under exclusion, then releases in one `finally`. Throws (`launch-unknown`, superseded control, unreconciled run) close its copy without clearing the predecessor. The supervisor/gate keep their own Unix copies until gate exit. A standalone Assignment follows the same handoff rule at its own settled result. If recording the handoff fails, retain the record, release the controller copy and attach `custody-handoff-not-recorded` to the returned result; a committed or settled outcome is preserved.

No child process starts inside the hot state mutex (`exec-under-hot-lock`): the host binary is resolved and the envelope built before any `withStateTx`.

**Controller implementation** (`src/run-supervisor/direct-launch.mjs`, called from `executeAssignment`). The sandbox's root is read-only, so the controller creates the capture files and `gate-exit.json` empty before the prepare and asks the sandbox driver to bind exactly those files writable (`attemptBinds`); the outbox is the one writable directory. The sandbox program leads `containment.bwrapPrefix` (the driver's prefix carries only its arguments). `spawnWithLocks` (holder-lock facade) hands the lock descriptions to the supervisor at 3 and 4; no other descriptor of the controller reaches it. After the result appears the controller still waits for `closed.json` (bounded) so the next dispatch never meets a step in flight; a supervisor that is gone while the agent lives is waited for through the adopt door. `controller/settle-context.json` carries what only the controller knows (effective policy, provider account evidence, fallback, stray-write baseline of the main checkout) to the settle step; `assignment.json` in the attempt directory is the effective assignment. A `supervise` for an attempt that already has a `supervisor-binding.json` or a `receipt.json` refuses with exit 71 `attempt-already-bound` before it touches any lock: its predecessor rule would otherwise end the live domain. The envelope's `deadlines.killWaitMs` (config `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs`) is the bound `kill_all` waits for an empty domain.

The controller does not settle while a supervisor lives. The controller reads receipts from files; it holds no handle to the supervisor.
